podcast.body: Released in 1995, this album followed the breakthrough success of Dookie. Its title was inspired by Billy Joe Armstrong's oldest son, Joey, who as a baby cried so much that he kept his parents awake all night. "When he was a baby, Joey, the oldest, cried so much that he kept dad and mom up all night. This is why Green Day's 95 album is called Insomniac."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Green Day: From their Beginning to 2005

podcast.body: Released in the fall of 1995, this album presented a heavier sound compared to its predecessor, Dookie. Its lyrics explored "doom and gloom" themes and displayed a more sarcastic tone than their previous work. Despite its heavier and more biting content, Insomniac remained an accessible record due to its strong song structures and melodies, effectively blending punk aggression with pop songwriting sensibilities. "Now if we dig into that record, it's a little heavier than Duckey, which is the previous record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
